questions.questionText:
All living organisms release energy from nutrient molecules within their cells.
What is the name of this characteristic?
Which level of organisation is shown by the heart of a mammal?

Female moths release chemicals into the air. Male moths detect these chemicals and fly towards
the females.
How do the chemicals spread through the air?

What are the smaller basic units of starch and glycogen molecules?
starch glycogen

options.text: amino acids fatty acids and glycerol

questions.questionText: What is the correct definition of an enzyme?

options.text: a carbohydrate that functions as a biological catalyst
a protein that functions as a biological catalyst
a substance that is changed by the reaction
a substance made of fats that changes the rate of a reaction

questions.questionText: Which statement describes the effect of temperature on enzymes?

options.text: High temperatures denature enzymes making it difficult for substrate molecules to fit into the active site.
High temperatures denature enzymes making it easy for substrate molecules to fit into the active site.
Low temperatures denature enzymes making it difficult for substrate molecules to fit into the active site.
Low temperatures denature enzymes making it easy for substrate molecules to fit into the active site.

rate of
photosynthesis
carbon dioxide
concentration
What could be the limiting factor of photosynthesis at X on the graph?
Which nutrient is required to prevent scurvy?
Which diagram represents the action of lipase?
In a double circulation, what is the role of the right side of the heart?

options.text: to receive oxygenated blood from the body and to pump oxygenated blood to the lungs
to receive oxygenated blood from the body and to pump deoxygenated blood to the lungs
to receive deoxygenated blood from the body and to pump oxygenated blood to the lungs
to receive deoxygenated blood from the body and to pump deoxygenated blood to the lungs

questions.questionText:
The photomicrograph shows some human blood cells.
What is the name of cell X and what is its function?
name function

Which row shows the action of muscles during inspiration?
internal external
diaphragm
intercostal muscles intercostal muscles
Which statement about urea is correct?

options.text: Amino acids are transported to the kidneys where they are converted to urea.
Urea travels from liver cells to the kidneys where it is filtered out of the blood.
Liver cells break down proteins to amino acids which are then converted to urea in the kidneys.
Urea is made in the kidneys and then removed from the body by the liver.

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows the junction between two neurones.
What is labelled at X?
What is the synthetic plant hormone 2,4-D used for?

Which statement about asexual reproduction would be a disadvantage for a farmer growing crop
plants?

options.text: Desirable qualities are shown throughout the crop.
Only one parent plant is required so growth is rapid.
All of the crop plants have the same risk of disease.

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows an abnormal sperm cell.
Why would the abnormal sperm cell be unable to fertilise an egg?

options.text: It has no acrosome so is unable to digest the jelly coat of the egg.
It has no mitochondria so lacks energy to swim to the egg.
It has no flagellum so cannot swim to the egg.
It has no nucleus so cannot fuse with the egg.

questions.questionText:
Some fruit flies have orange eyes and others have red eyes.
If two orange-eyed fruit flies are crossed, their offspring always have orange eyes.
If two red-eyed fruit flies are crossed, their offspring can have orange eyes or red eyes.
What can be concluded from these observations?

options.text: The allele for orange eyes is dominant.
The allele for orange eyes is recessive.
The alleles for orange and red eyes are codominant.
This is an example of sex linkage.

questions.questionText:
Sickle cell anaemia is a genetic disorder which results in severe illness in homozygous
individuals. In some human populations, being heterozygous can be beneficial.
What could be the reason for this?

options.text: Heterozygous individuals are not affected by the disorder.
Heterozygous individuals are more resistant to malaria.
The disorder is caused by a dominant allele.

questions.questionText: Which statement about selective breeding is correct?

options.text: It involves a struggle for survival.
It always involves only one parent.
It involves parents that possess desirable features.

questions.questionText: What is the name of an organism that obtains its energy from dead organic material?

A herd of red deer live in a forest that contains snakes and a large variety of birds.
Which group of organisms is an example of a population?

options.text: all the animals in the forest
all the red deer in the forest
all the organisms in the forest
all the plants in the forest

questions.questionText: With which kingdoms do bacteria share the same genetic code?
Which process makes use of a genetically engineered organism?

options.text: using enzymes in biological washing powders
using pectinase in fruit juice production

questions.questionText: What is a reason for conserving plant species?

options.text: to absorb oxygen from the air
to obtain drugs for medicinal use
to release carbon dioxide into the air

questions.questionText:
The food web shows the feeding relationships in a woodland.
sparrowhawks
chaffinches
grey wood
squirrels pigeons
caterpillars
trees
If all the chaffinches in the food web die, which effect would this have?

options.text: The amount of damage to trees will increase.
The food supply for grey squirrels will increase.
The number of wood pigeons will increase.

The population of caterpillars will decrease.
